title: Component form of a normalized descent universal property
statement: Let A,B,C be categories, L:A to B, F:B to C and T:A to C functors, and e:L followed by F isomorphic to T. Suppose that for every G:B to C and c:L followed by G isomorphic to T there exists a unique i:F isomorphic to G such that whiskering i by L and composing with c gives e. Then for each such G,c there exists a unique i:F isomorphic to G such that, for every P of A, i(L(P)) equals e(P) followed by the inverse of c(P). This categorical consequence is applied to the existing integralPullbackDescent universal field; it adds no new universal-property assumption there.

source.place: Tag 099N(5), normalized derived pullback descent; component reformulation of IntegralPullbackDescent.universal.

proof.text: Apply the universal-property hypothesis to G and c. Evaluate its compatibility equation at P and cancel c(P) to get the component formula. Conversely, compose each proposed component formula with c(P), cancel the inverse, and use natural-transformation extensionality to recover the full compatibility equation. Apply the uniqueness clause from the universal-property hypothesis. This is a complete proof in arbitrary categories, including empty representative categories; no sheaf or coefficient assertion is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedDescentComponents_existsUnique
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B]
    {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} C]
    (L : A ⥤ B) (F : B ⥤ C) (T : A ⥤ C) (e : L ⋙ F ≅ T)
    (universal : ∀ (G : B ⥤ C) (c : L ⋙ G ≅ T),
      ∃! i : F ≅ G, Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L i ≪≫ c = e)
    (G : B ⥤ C) (c : L ⋙ G ≅ T) :
    ∃! i : F ≅ G, ∀ P : A, i.app (L.obj P) = e.app P ≪≫ (c.app P).symm
